question: Which developmental trait makes toddlers particularly prone to poisoning?

options.A: Their natural urge to taste and mouth objects
options.D: An advanced ability to read warning labels

explanation: Young children explore their environment by putting items directly into their mouths, which puts them at high risk of swallowing harmful substances. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why does a toxic substance usually cause more severe harm in a toddler than in an adult?

options.A: The digestive system of a child completely neutralizes poisons
options.B: The smaller body mass of a child increases concentration effects
options.C: Adults absorb chemicals through the skin much quicker than children
options.D: Children have fully matured internal organs that process toxins faster

explanation: Because a child weighs much less than an adult, even a tiny amount of a toxic substance creates a dangerously high concentration in their small body. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is a frequent cause of accidental chemical ingestion in many homes?

options.A: Storing dangerous liquids inside empty beverage bottles
options.B: Placing clear warning signs written in local languages
options.C: Keeping all cleaning agents locked inside high steel cabinets
options.D: Using factory-sealed safety caps on every medication bottle

explanation: Transferring harmful chemicals like kerosene or bleach into drink bottles tricks children into thinking the liquid is safe to consume. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h2)

question: A mother in the community stores her cooking oil and a bottle of caustic soda solution side by side on the floor. What is the most appropriate safety action to advise?

options.A: Relocate the caustic soda to a locked, high cupboard out of reach
options.B: Leave the items on the floor but place a cloth over them
options.C: Instruct the older siblings to watch the toddler near the floor
options.D: Tell the mother to taste the liquid before using it in meals

explanation: Dangerous chemicals must always be stored completely out of a child's reach, ideally in a locked enclosure, rather than left at floor level. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is a direct physical sign of swallowing a corrosive chemical?

options.A: An inability to blink the eyelids
options.B: Rapid growth of fingernails within hours
options.C: Burns or redness around the lips and oral cavity
options.D: Sudden loss of hearing in both ears

explanation: Corrosive substances burn the delicate tissues they touch first, leaving visible chemical burns around the mouth and lips. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why is diagnosing household poisoning sometimes difficult for caregivers and healthcare workers?

options.A: Poisoning never causes any visible physical changes in the body
options.B: Toxins only begin affecting the body after exactly three days
options.C: Children always describe exactly what they swallowed when asked
options.D: Early symptoms often mimic common illnesses like stomach upsets

explanation: Because vomiting and lethargy happen with many ordinary sicknesses, caregivers may not immediately realize the child has ingested a toxic substance. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h3)

question: What dangerous practice must midwives actively discourage when a child swallows kerosene or bleach?

options.A: Keeping the child calm while arranging transport
options.B: Inducing vomiting or giving home concoctions like palm oil
options.C: Bringing the empty product container to the hospital
options.D: Washing the child's face with cool running water

explanation: Forcing a child to vomit corrosive chemicals or petroleum products causes severe secondary damage to the esophagus and lungs. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h4)

question: A toddler drinks a mouthful of concentrated liquid bleach. The mother wants to make the child vomit immediately. What should the midwife advise?

options.A: Tell the mother to give extra palm oil to neutralize the bleach
options.B: Advise the mother to wait two hours before trying any home remedies
options.C: Encourage the mother to use salt water to speed up the vomiting
options.D: Stop the mother, because vomiting will cause more damage to the throat

explanation: Corrosive liquids burn the throat on the way down; forcing them back up causes a second chemical burn on the sensitive tissues. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h4)

question: How should pot and pan handles be positioned on a stove to prevent burns?

options.A: Turned inward toward the back of the stove
options.B: Hanging outward over the edge of the stove
options.C: Balanced vertically above the open flame
options.D: Removed entirely while cooking hot food

explanation: Turning handles inward prevents toddlers from accidentally bumping or pulling hot pots down onto themselves. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which strategy best prevents drowning incidents involving toddlers inside a home?

options.A: Relying on older siblings to watch water containers outdoors
options.B: Leaving bathroom doors wide open to improve home ventilation
options.C: Keeping all water storage buckets and drums tightly covered
options.D: Teaching every six-month-old infant how to swim independently

explanation: Toddlers can drown in just a few inches of standing water in an uncovered bucket, making secure covers essential. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h5)

question: During which routine contact can midwives effectively educate mothers on home safety?

options.D: Annual financial audits of local hospitals

explanation: Postnatal and immunization clinics bring mothers and babies directly to the midwife, providing a perfect opportunity to discuss home safety. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important for midwives to use local languages and practical demonstrations during safety talks?

options.A: It is a strict requirement for writing formal medical research papers
options.B: It ensures mothers easily understand and apply the safety rules
options.C: It replaces the need for physical inspections of family houses
options.D: It prevents mothers from asking questions about home care

explanation: Clear, local communication helps bridge educational gaps and ensures families can realistically adopt accident prevention measures. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T3#BMP222_U4_T3_h6)
